title: The hot new pinned iPhone contact is an AI agent
excerpt: Techies are filling their pinned text message slots with AI agents. Agents like Instinct, Fo, and Flip claimed a spot.
content_html:
We asked 6 techies to show us their pinned iPhone contacts. AI agents dominated.

By Henry Chandonnet

You're currently following this author! Click to unsubscribe from email alerts.

2026-11-28T09:55:01.320Z

In case of emergency, text my AI agent.

Many iPhone users have pinned text chats in their Messages app. Maybe you pin your partner, parent, or gossipy group chat. It makes navigation easy.

There's a new texter in the game: AI agents. Some of these, like Meta's Muse, require whole new apps. Others function right there in Messages, and might be a high enough priority to deserve one of nine pin slots.

Business Insider asked six techies — from investors to founders — to show off their pins. Spoiler: AI agents were everywhere.

David Pawlan, growth lead at Merit Systems

Pawlan has a special reason to have lots of AI agents: he tests them for work.

The 29-year-old from New York runs an "Assistant Benchmark" that ranks the helpfulness of each AI agent. He uses all nine of his pins for them; no humans needed.

"I'm using all of the agents for the same purpose," he said. "I run the same tests across all of them to compare performance so there isn't a differentiation of what I do with each agent."

Philippe Mallette, investor at Flourish Ventures

Mallette's pinned texts are also 100% AI, 0% human.

First is Fo by Wajo, which he called his "everything assistant." Then there's Hark, which he uses mainly for purchases and proactivity. It recently reminded the 27-year-old from San Francisco of a concert he had on his calendar but hadn't yet bought tickets for.

Then there's Town, which Mallette said was great because of its pre-built email workflows. These make the agent "feel very capable without much teaching," he said.

Those are his consistent agents. He's also always testing something new — in this case, the AI money manager Flip.

Niki Victoria, founder of Photogenik

Victoria has two agents in her pinned chats — but only one is AI.

The so-called "assistant," giving out a little fist bump, is Instinct. "I text it to book flights, send gifts, set reminders, and brainstorm a quick post," the 24-year-old from New York said.

Then there's her DBA group chat. This is for Victoria's human agents, the ones who help her land brand deals as a creator. The third pin is Abraham Sameer, her cofounder. "This chat never sleeps," she said.

Victoria also uses the agent Boardy for LinkedIn and X networking. It wasn't worthy of a pin, though; in the screenshot she sent Business Insider, it was six chats down.

Stanley Virgint, founder of Soar

Virgint's startup is a texting agent for travel. It's placed front and center on his Messages app.

The 26-year-old has several humans in his pins: his mom, family, and his team at work. Then there's Flip, which he uses to track his finances. The agent also tells him whether to invest more.

222 is his social agent. It's helped Virgint meet people after moving to San Francisco, he said. "It's been a good way to get out of my work circles, and it's really good at putting interesting strangers in a room together," he said.

And then there's his agent to find more agents. He uses the Agent Store pin to keep track of new AI texting tools and gets a weekly roundup of what's launching.

"There are so many cool agents launching it's hard to keep up!" he said.

Ken Wattana, founder of Conto

Wattana only has one pinned chat, and he hasn't even saved its contact information.

"The first personal assistant to really work properly is the one that's earned my trust," the 33-year-old from San Francisco said. "Instinct."
